aiOverview.content: A standard, used PlayStation 2 (PS2) console generally holds a value between $80 and $200, depending on condition, model (Fat vs. Slim), and included accessories. Loose consoles often sell for around $90, while complete-in-box (CIB) units range from $130 to over $200. Rare, limited-edition consoles or factory-sealed, new units can be worth significantly more, sometimes exceeding $1,000. Key Factors Affecting PS2 Value Condition and Bundle: Clean consoles with original controllers, cables, and a memory card (a complete bundle) are at the higher end of the price range ($150-$200+). Model Variants: Standard Fat/Slim: Generally $80–$130 for a used, working console. Special Editions: Colors like Sakura Pink, Gold, or special bundles (e.g., Final Fantasy XII) can sell for $200-$500 or more. Market Trends: Prices have risen due to nostalgia, with many collectors seeking out the console. Rare Games: While the console itself is common, specific rare titles can significantly increase the value of a bundle. For a quick sale, GameStop offers roughly $65 in cash or $93 in store credit as of early 2026. GameStop
